claim: Whole mount GFP immunofluorescence of RARECreERT2; mTmG embryos induced at E7.5 and sacrificed at E10.5 revealed efficient labeling of the forebrain.
source: Whole mount GFP immunofluorescence (IF) of embryos induced at E7.5 and sacrificed at E10.5 revealed efficient labeling of the forebrain (Figure 1C and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 1C and Video 1.

claim: Analysis of RARECreERT2; mTmG whole embryo sections at E11.5 after tamoxifen administration at E7.5 and E8.5 revealed efficient and consistent labeling of various well-known RA-responsive organs such as the lungs, liver, spinal cord, heart, and differentiating somites.
source: Analysis of whole embryo sections by GFP IF revealed efficient and consistent labeling of various well-known RA-responsive organs such as the lungs (Malpel et al., 2000), liver (Brade et al., 2011), spinal cord (Sockanathan and Jessell, 1998), heart (Niederreither et al., 2001; Niederreither et al., 2002a), and differentiating somites (Rossant et al., 1991; Niederreither et al., 1999; Diez del Corral et al., 2003; Duester, 2007) in all embryos analyzed (Figure 1D).

claim: Somite-specific labeling was detected with a single pulse at E8.5 followed by analysis at E11.5.
source: Somite-specific labeling, as revealed by co-IF for MyoD and GFP, was also detected with a single pulse at E8.5 followed by analysis at E11.5 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Analysis of E9.5 RARECreERT2 embryos stained with X-gal after TAM treatment at E6.5 revealed specific labeling of the venous pole derivatives (atria and outflow tract).
source: A closer look at the hearts of E9.5 RARECreERT2 embryos stained with X-gal after TAM treatment at E6.5 revealed specific labeling of the venous pole derivatives (atria and outflow tract) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), and minimal labeling of the developing ventricles, faithfully recapitulating the pattern observed with other RA reporters (Rossant et al., 1991; Dollé et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Minimal labeling of the developing ventricles was observed in E9.5 RARECreERT2 embryos after TAM treatment at E6.5.
source: A closer look at the hearts of E9.5 RARECreERT2 embryos stained with X-gal after TAM treatment at E6.5 revealed specific labeling of the venous pole derivatives (atria and outflow tract) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), and minimal labeling of the developing ventricles, faithfully recapitulating the pattern observed with other RA reporters (Rossant et al., 1991; Dollé et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Embryos pulsed with tamoxifen at E10.5 and analyzed at E13.5 exhibited very strong labeling of the heart ventricles with almost no labeling of the atria and outflow tract.
source: Meanwhile, embryos pulsed with tamoxifen at E10.5 and analyzed at E13.5 exhibited very strong labeling of the heart ventricles with almost no labeling of the atria and outflow tract (Figure 2B), once again consistent with previously published data (Moss et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2B, supported by citation to Moss et al., 1998.

claim: Analysis of E13.5 heart sections counterstained with eosin revealed the majority of the X-gal labeling to be within the myocardial wall of the heart and not the epicardium.
source: Interestingly, analysis of E13.5 heart sections counterstained with eosin revealed the majority of the X-gal labeling to be within the myocardial wall of the heart and not the epicardium (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Administration of tamoxifen at E9.5 to RARECreERT2; mTmG embryos followed by analysis at E11.5 revealed GFP localization in both WT1+ and MF20+ cells.
source: Administration of tamoxifen at E9.5 followed by analysis at E11.5 revealed GFP localization in both WT1+ and MF20+ cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Tamoxifen administration at E10.5 followed by analysis at E13.5 revealed high labeling of MF20+ cardiomyocytes, but only minor labeling of WT1+ epicardial cells.
source: Meanwhile, tamoxifen administration at E10.5 followed by analysis at E13.5 revealed high labeling of MF20+ cardiomyocytes, but only minor labeling of WT1+ epicardial cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The cardiomyocyte-specific labeling was highest in the compact layer, with minimal GFP+ cells observed in trabecular cardiomyocytes.
source: The cardiomyocyte-specific labeling was highest in the compact layer, with minimal GFP+ cells observed in trabecular cardiomyocytes (Figure 2D, left panel).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2D.

claim: As heart development proceeds, cardiomyocyte precursors of the compact layer increasingly become the major RA-responsive cell-type.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that as heart development proceeds, cardiomyocyte precursors of the compact layer increasingly become the major RA-responsive cell-type.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: Administration of RA to pregnant dams at E10.5 4 hr prior to TAM induction increased the RA-response in RARECreERT2 hearts analyzed at E13.5.
source: Administration of RA to pregnant dams at E10.5 4 hr prior to TAM induction increased the RA-response in RARECreERT2 hearts analyzed at E13.5, even labeling a substantial portion of trabecular myocytes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Treatment of embryos with the RAR inverse agonist BMS493 prior to and following tamoxifen administration led to a very strong decrease in GFP+ cells.
source: Conversely, treatment of embryos with the RAR inverse agonist BMS493 (Germain et al., 2009) prior to and following tamoxifen administration led to a very strong decrease in GFP+ cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Isolation of primary cardiomyocytes from E18.5 RARECreERT2 hearts followed by RA treatment led to specific labeling of Troponin T+ cardiomyocytes.
source: Moreover, isolation of primary cardiomyocytes from E18.5 RARECreERT2 hearts followed by RA treatment led to specific labeling of Troponin T+ cardiomyocytes (Figure 2G, schematic and Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2H.

claim: RA treatment in cultured cardiomyocytes led to upregulation of the RA target genes Rarb, Rbp1, and Cyp26a1.
source: The efficiency of the RA treatment in cultured cardiomyocytes was confirmed by qPCR analysis, which showed upregulation of the RA target genes Rarb, Rbp1 (retinol binding protein), and Cyp26a1 (cytochrome P450 family 26 subfamily a polypeptide 1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: GFP+ cells could be detected as early as 28 hr after RA treatment in primary cardiomyocytes, with peak levels at 48 hr.
source: First, we treated primary cardiomyocytes isolated from RARECreERT2; mTmG hearts with 10 nM RA for different periods of time (8–48 hr) and found that GFP+ cells could be detected as early as 28 hr, with peak levels at 48 hr.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Treated cardiomyocytes showed a dose-dependent response to RA.
source: Next, we treated cardiomyocytes with increasing doses of RA (0.1–1000 ng/ml) for 48 hr and quantified the number of GFP+ cells. Treated cardiomyocytes showed a dose-dependent response to RA (Figure 2I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: GFP+ cells could be detected with very low doses of RA (0.1 nM – 1 nM) in primary cardiomyocytes.
source: Strikingly, GFP+ cells could also be detected with very low doses of RA (0.1 nM – 1 nM) (Figure 2I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Cardiomyocytes are highly responsive to exogenous RA treatment at physiologically relevant levels.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that cardiomyocytes are highly responsive to exogenous RA treatment at physiologically relevant levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: A second RARECreERT2 line (Line B) showed a nearly identical pattern of GFP staining in the compact myocardium when compared to the original line.
source: Administration of tamoxifen at E10.5 followed by analysis at E14.5 revealed a nearly identical pattern of GFP staining in the compact myocardium when compared to our original line (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The cardiomyocyte-specific labeling observed with the RARECreERT2 line is a reliable response that can be influenced by exogenous activation or inactivation of the RA pathway.
source: Altogether, these data demonstrate that the cardiomyocyte-specific labeling observed with the RARECreERT2 line is a reliable response that can be influenced by exogenous activation or inactivation of the RA pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: It is unclear whether retinoids continue to play an important role after E13.5 in heart development.
source: Although the role of RA signaling during heart looping and myocardial compaction is well described, it is unclear whether retinoids continue to play an important role after E13.5 (Zaffran et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge, supported by citation to Zaffran et al., 2014.

claim: A high number of GFP+ cells, mainly cardiomyocytes, were observed in RARECreERT2 hearts after tamoxifen administration at E14.5 and analysis at E18.5.
source: We next decided to look at later time-points of heart development by administering tamoxifen at E14.5 and sacrificing embryos at E18.5. Strikingly, we observed a high number of GFP+ cells, mainly cardiomyocytes (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Many of the labeled cells were located deep within the compact layer in RARECreERT2 hearts after tamoxifen administration at E14.5 and analysis at E18.5.
source: We also noticed that many of the labeled cells were located deep within the compact layer (Figure 3A, white arrows), a striking observation given that at these time-points ALDH1A2 protein is believed to be restricted to the epicardium (Moss et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3A, with reference to Moss et al., 1998.

claim: ALDH1A2 protein is believed to be restricted to the epicardium at E14.5-E18.5.
source: We also noticed that many of the labeled cells were located deep within the compact layer (Figure 3A, white arrows), a striking observation given that at these time-points ALDH1A2 protein is believed to be restricted to the epicardium (Moss et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Moss et al., 1998.

claim: Cardiomyocyte-specific labeling was observed both near the epicardium as well as deeper within the myocardial wall after tamoxifen administration at E15.5 and analysis at E17.5.
source: To see if this deep labeling was simply due to clonal expansion of cardiomyocytes located near the epicardium, we traced cells for a shorter period of time by giving a pulse at E15.5 and analyzing at E17.5. Once again, we observed cardiomyocyte-specific labeling, both near the epicardium as well as deeper within the myocardial wall (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Many of the GFP+ cardiomyocytes located away from the epicardium were separated from other cells.
source: Many of the GFP+ cardiomyocytes located away from the epicardium were separated from other cells (Figure 3B, white arrows), suggesting their response arises from a local source of RA, independently of the epicardium.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The RA response of cardiomyocytes located away from the epicardium arises from a local source of RA, independently of the epicardium.
source: Many of the GFP+ cardiomyocytes located away from the epicardium were separated from other cells (Figure 3B, white arrows), suggesting their response arises from a local source of RA, independently of the epicardium.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: At E12.5 ALDH1A2 was restricted to the epicardium.
source: At E12.5 ALDH1A2 was, as previously shown, restricted to the epicardium.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, consistent with previous literature.

claim: After E14.5, ALDH1A2 could be detected within the ventricular and interventricular walls.
source: After E14.5, however, ALDH1A2 could be detected within the ventricular and interventricular walls.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: ALDH1A2 expression pattern increased at later time-points, peaking at E18.5.
source: This expression pattern increased at later time-points, peaking at E18.5 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3C.

claim: No co-IF of ALDH1A2 with cardiomyocyte (MF20), smooth muscle (Transgelin) or endothelial (PECAM1) markers was detected.
source: To determine which cell-types were positive for ALDH1A2 we performed co-IF with various antibodies. No co-IF of ALDH1A2 with cardiomyocyte (MF20) (data not shown), smooth muscle (Transgelin) (data not shown) or endothelial (PECAM1) (Figure 3D) markers was detected.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ALDH1A2+ cells were positive for the intermediate filament marker Vimentin, suggesting them to be cardiac fibroblasts or connective tissue.
source: By contrast, ALDH1A2+ cells were positive for the intermediate filament marker Vimentin, suggesting them to be cardiac fibroblasts or connective tissue (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A significant portion of ALDH1A2+ cells within the ventricular wall were labeled with GFP in WT1CreERT2; mTmG embryos after tamoxifen induction at E10.5 and analysis at E16.5, demonstrating they originate from the epicardium.
source: Tamoxifen induction at E10.5 followed by analysis at E16.5 revealed a significant portion of ALDH1A2+ cells within the ventricular wall were labeled with GFP, demonstrating they indeed originate from the epicardium (Figure 3E, white arrows).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Epicardial cells and epicardial-derived cardiac fibroblasts that have migrated into deeper layers of the forming myocardium produce ALDH1A2, and the local RA signal is received by neighboring cardiomyocytes.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that epicardial cells and epicardial-derived cardiac fibroblasts that have migrated into deeper layers of the forming myocardium produce ALDH1A2, and that the local RA signal is received by neighboring cardiomyocytes (Figure 3F, schematic).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study as shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Analysis of RARECreERT2; mTmG hearts 6 days after MI revealed drastic GFP enrichment in infarct hearts when compared to sham controls.
source: Strikingly, analysis of hearts 6 days after MI revealed drastic GFP enrichment in infarct hearts when compared to sham controls (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ALDH1A2 protein and mRNA levels were enriched in infarcted hearts.
source: ALDH1A2 protein and mRNA levels were also enriched in infarcted hearts as shown by IF and qPCR analysis, respectively (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: The staining pattern of GFP closely overlapped with ALDH1A2 in infarcted hearts, suggesting it to be the major enzyme driving the RA response.
source: Interestingly, the staining pattern of GFP closely overlapped with ALDH1A2, suggesting it to be the major enzyme driving the RA response in infarct hearts, which is consistent with previous studies (Kikuchi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study, supported by citation to Kikuchi et al., 2011.

claim: Aldh1a1 and Aldh1a3 mRNA levels were upregulated in infarcted hearts.
source: Aldh1a1 and Aldh1a3 mRNA levels were also upregulated as determined by qPCR analysis (Figure 4C); however, we could not detect ALDH1A1/A3 protein by IF using commercial antibodies (data not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4C.

claim: An increase in the number of ALDH1A2+ and GFP+ cells was observed particularly within the injury and border zones of damage in infarcted hearts.
source: A closer look at the staining patterns of ALDH1A2 and GFP revealed an increase in the number of positive cells particularly within the injury and border zones of damage (Figure 4B, F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4B and 4F.

claim: Most ALDH1A2+ cells were GFP-negative in infarcted hearts.
source: Most ALDH1A2+ cells were GFP-negative (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Many different cell-types were responsive to RA in infarcted hearts, including PECAM1+ coronary vessels, αSMA+ activated fibroblasts and/or smooth muscle cells and Troponin T+ cardiomyocytes.
source: Co-IF for GFP with various markers demonstrated that many different cell-types were responsive to RA. These included PECAM1+ coronary vessels, αSMA+ activated fibroblasts and/or smooth muscle cells and Troponin T+ cardiomyocytes (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4E.

claim: A substantial portion of cardiomyocytes in the injury border zone were GFP+ in infarcted hearts.
source: Interestingly, a substantial portion of cardiomyocytes in the injury border zone, a region that is highly remodeled after MI, were also GFP+ (Figure 4G, white arrows).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 4G.

claim: IF analysis demonstrated decreased ALDH1A2 immunoreactivity in RAKO hearts 6 days post MI.
source: IF analysis demonstrated decreased ALDH1A2 immunoreactivity in RAKO hearts 6 days post MI (Figure 5B), and qPCR analysis revealed reasonable deletion efficiency, with around 70 % decrease of Aldh1a1 and Aldh1a2 mRNA levels (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5B.

claim: qPCR analysis revealed around 70% decrease of Aldh1a1 and Aldh1a2 mRNA levels in RAKO hearts 6 days post MI.
source: IF analysis demonstrated decreased ALDH1A2 immunoreactivity in RAKO hearts 6 days post MI (Figure 5B), and qPCR analysis revealed reasonable deletion efficiency, with around 70 % decrease of Aldh1a1 and Aldh1a2 mRNA levels (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Aldh1a3 mRNA levels were not significantly downregulated in RAKO hearts 6 days post MI.
source: Aldh1a3 mRNA levels were not significantly downregulated (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Incomplete deletion of Aldh1a genes was likely due to epigenetic silencing of their loci, since they are not actively expressed in adult hearts prior to MI.
source: Incomplete deletion of Aldh1a genes was likely due to epigenetic silencing of their loci, since they are not actively expressed in adult hearts prior to MI (Kikuchi et al., 2011; this study).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study, supported by citation to Kikuchi et al., 2011.

claim: PCR analysis of genomic DNA from mutant MI hearts revealed incomplete excision of Aldh1a2 and Aldh1a3 floxed alleles.
source: Consistently, PCR analysis of genomic DNA from mutant MI hearts revealed incomplete excision of Aldh1a2 and Aldh1a3 floxed alleles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: The low recombination was not due to poor activity of the CAGGCreER line, which showed very efficient recombination in the adult heart when crossed with the Rosa26 based mTmG reporter.
source: The low recombination was not due to poor activity of the CAGGCreER line, which, upon crossing with the Rosa26 based mTmG reporter, showed very efficient recombination in the adult heart (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F-G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1F-G.

claim: RAKO mice exhibited significantly increased infarct zones as revealed by collagen staining with Sirius red.
source: Strikingly, RAKO mice exhibited significantly increased infarct zones as revealed by collagen staining with Sirius red (Figure 5D–E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5D-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: RAKO mice showed increased rates of apoptosis as determined by active caspase three and TUNEL staining.
source: Furthermore, RAKO mice showed increased rates of apoptosis as determined by active caspase three and TUNEL (Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling) staining (Figure 5F–G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5F-G.

claim: No apoptosis was observed in RAKO mice subjected to sham surgery.
source: No apoptosis was observed in RAKO mice subjected to sham surgery (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Many of the apoptotic cells in RAKO mice were cardiomyocytes and they tended to concentrate in clusters or 'patches' that were positive for both active caspase3 and TUNEL.
source: Interestingly, many of the apoptotic cells in RAKO mice were cardiomyocytes and they tended to concentrate in clusters or so called 'patches' that were positive for both active caspase3 and TUNEL (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Apoptotic patches were observed in 5 out of 10 RAKO mice and only 1 out of 11 control mice.
source: These patches were observed in 5 out of 10 RAKO mice and only 1 out of 11 control mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D, table).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D.

claim: RAKO mice exhibited higher mortality rates (Early death: RAKO 4 of 14 vs. CTL 0 of 11) before analysis at 6 days post MI.
source: Moreover, RAKO mice exhibited higher mortality rates (Early death: RAKO 4 of 14 vs. CTL 0 of 11) before analysis at 6 days post MI (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D, table).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Dampening the RA response prior to MI leads to increased cardiomyocyte apoptosis and mortality.
source: Thus, dampening the RA response prior to MI leads to increased cardiomyocyte apoptosis and mortality, suggesting RA signaling plays a protective role in damaged heart muscle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: RA signaling plays a protective role in damaged heart muscle.
source: Thus, dampening the RA response prior to MI leads to increased cardiomyocyte apoptosis and mortality, suggesting RA signaling plays a protective role in damaged heart muscle.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: A previous study suggested that the RA pathway reduced apoptosis in damaged hearts by modulating the MAP kinase pathway through direct transcriptional regulation of Adam10.
source: A previous study using exogenous RA supplementation in mice subjected to ischaemia/reperfusion determined that the RA pathway reduced apoptosis in damaged hearts by modulating the MAP kinase pathway. This was suggested to be through direct transcriptional regulation of Adam10, a gene which encodes for a protease that cleaves and inactivates the RAGE10 (Receptor for Advanced Glycation End products) receptor, a positive regulator of the ERK1/2 MAP kinase pathway (Zhu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2015.

claim: No differences in ERK1/2 activation were observed in RAKO mice as determined by IF for phospho-ERK1/2.
source: However, we did not observe any differences in ERK1/2 activation, as determined by IF for phospho-ERK1/2, in our RAKO mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-B.

claim: Treatment of primary cardiomyocytes with RA or BMS493 did not lead to significant changes in Adam10 expression.
source: Additionally, treatment of primary cardiomyocytes with RA or BMS493 did not lead to significant changes in Adam10 expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C-D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C-D.

claim: The anti-apoptotic effects of RA observed in the RAKO model are unrelated to Adam10/MAP-Kinase signaling.
source: Taken together, these data suggest the anti-apoptotic effects of RA observed in our model of RA depletion to be unrelated to Adam10/MAP-Kinase signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented in the study.

claim: Analysis of the RNA sequencing data identified several canonical RA targets such as Rarb, Cyp26b1 and Cyp26a1 to be top hits among all genes analyzed.
source: Analysis of the sequencing data identified several canonical RA targets such as Rarb, Cyp26b1 and Cyp26a1 to be top hits among all genes analyzed (Figure 6B, Supplementary file 1), and gene ontology analysis revealed enrichment of GO terms for inflammatory and DNA damage responses (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6B and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Gene ontology analysis revealed enrichment of GO terms for inflammatory and DNA damage responses in RA-treated cardiomyocytes.
source: Analysis of the sequencing data identified several canonical RA targets such as Rarb, Cyp26b1 and Cyp26a1 to be top hits among all genes analyzed (Figure 6B, Supplementary file 1), and gene ontology analysis revealed enrichment of GO terms for inflammatory and DNA damage responses (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Several genes previously shown to be important in cardiac development and MI were determined to be either up or downregulated in RA-treated cardiomyocytes.
source: Furthermore, several genes previously shown to be important in cardiac development and MI were also determined to be either up or downregulated (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Tgm2 was significantly upregulated in RA-treated cardiomyocytes.
source: Of note, Tgm2, which has been shown to promote ATP synthesis and thus limit damage after MI, was significantly upregulated (Figure 6B; Szondy et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6B, supported by citation to Szondy et al., 2006.

claim: Tgm2 has been shown to promote ATP synthesis and thus limit damage after MI.
source: Of note, Tgm2, which has been shown to promote ATP synthesis and thus limit damage after MI, was significantly upregulated (Figure 6B; Szondy et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Szondy et al., 2006.

claim: RA treatment significantly repressed the expression of Angiotensin converting enzyme 1 (Ace1) in cardiomyocytes.
source: We also noticed that RA treatment significantly repressed the expression of Angiotensin converting enzyme 1 (Ace1) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6B.

claim: ACE1 is responsible for converting angiotensin 1 into angiotensin 2, which in turn activates the renin angiotensin system and subsequent vasoconstriction.
source: ACE1 is responsible for converting angiotensin 1 into angiotensin 2, which in turn activates the renin angiotensin system and subsequent vasoconstriction.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ACE1.

claim: Upregulation of ACE1 has been observed in rodent hearts after MI and is generally considered to be harmful.
source: Upregulation of ACE1 has been observed in rodent hearts after MI and is generally considered to be harmful (Sun, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sun, 2010.

claim: ACE inhibitors are commonly used to treat patients recovering from MI, and they have shown great success in various clinical trials.
source: Indeed, ACE inhibitors are commonly used to treat patients recovering from MI, and they have shown great success in various clinical trials (Flather et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Flather et al., 2000.

claim: A connection between RA signaling, the RAS system, and cardiomyocyte-specific apoptosis has been previously established in vitro.
source: Moreover, a connection between RA signaling, the RAS system, and cardiomyocyte-specific apoptosis has been previously established in vitro (Palm-Leis et al., 2004; Guleria et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Palm-Leis et al., 2004; Guleria et al., 2011.

claim: Activation and repression of Tgm2 and Ace1 after 48 hr RA treatment was confirmed by qPCR analysis.
source: Respective activation and repression of Tgm2 and Ace1 after 48 hr RA treatment was confirmed by qPCR analysis (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Tgm2 and Ace1 modulation by RA signaling was also observed with 9-hr RA-treatment.
source: Tgm2 and Ace1 modulation by RA signaling was also observed with 9-hr RA-treatment (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Treatment of cardiomyocytes with BMS493 for 48 hr resulted in repression of Tgm2 expression and increase in Ace1 levels.
source: Next, we treated cardiomyocytes with BMS493 for 48 hr, and observed that Tgm2 expression was repressed while Ace1 levels were increased, consistent with our hypothesis that both genes are regulated by RA signaling (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6F.

claim: RA treatment repressed Ace1 expression in cardiomyocytes after removal of endothelial cells.
source: To address this issue, we removed endothelial cells from our cardiomyocyte cultures using CD31 magnetic beads, then treated enriched cardiomyocytes with RA for 48 hr (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-B). Consistently, RA treatment repressed Ace1 expression (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6G and Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Tgm2 and Ace1 were upregulated in MI hearts when compared to sham controls.
source: Tgm2 and Ace1 were also upregulated in MI hearts when compared to sham controls (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: No changes in Tgm2 or Ace1 expression were detected with 3 hr RA treatment with or without cycloheximide, suggesting that Tgm2 and Ace1 are indirect RA targets.
source: Finally, to see if Tgm2 and Ace1 are direct or indirect RA targets, we treated cultured cardiomyocytes with RA for only 3 hours and added the translational inhibitor cycloheximide to block non-specific activation of Tgm2/Ace1. No changes in Tgm2 or Ace1 expression were detected with the 3 hr RA treatment with or without cycloheximide, suggesting that Tgm2 and Ace1 are indirect RA targets.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Rarb expression was still activated by 3 hr RA treatment with or without cycloheximide.
source: Importantly, Rarb expression was still activated by 3 hr RA treatment with or without cycloheximide (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2D.
